steps.instr: Say it another way: complete the second sentence with the word in capitals, so it means the same.
steps.o: It doesn't matter if it's Rome or Tokyo — I never sleep well the first night.
steps.post: I never sleep well the first night.
steps.n: no matter where = wherever; keep “where”: not “no matter I travel”

steps.instr: Say it another way: complete the second sentence with the word in capitals, so it means the same.
steps.o: Since I stopped commuting, I've had lots of free time and nothing to fill it with.
steps.pre: Since I stopped commuting, I've had
steps.a: a lot of time on my hands
acc: a lot of time on my hands
lots of time on my hands
a lot more time on my hands
so much time on my hands
plenty of time on my hands
a lot of free time on my hands
steps.n: time on my hands = free time and nothing to fill it with; “on”, not “in”

steps.instr: Say it another way: complete the second sentence with the word in capitals, so it means the same.
steps.o: I use GPS far too much, even to get to the supermarket.
steps.post: , even to get to the supermarket.
steps.a: rely on GPS way more than I should
acc: rely on GPS way more than I should
rely on GPS much more than I should
rely on GPS more than I should
rely on GPS a lot more than I should
rely on GPS far more than I should
rely on GPS way too much
rely way too much on GPS
steps.n: rely on sth more than I should = I need it or use it too much; “way more” = much more (informal)

steps.instr: Say it another way: complete the second sentence with the word in capitals, so it means the same.
steps.o: Whatever the weather's like, my neighbor cycles to work every day.
steps.pre: My neighbor cycles to work every day,
steps.n: come rain or shine = whatever the weather; it can also start the sentence: “Come rain or shine, my neighbor…”

steps.instr: Say it another way: complete the second sentence with the word in capitals, so it means the same.
steps.o: I don't know why, but I always feel at home in this old bookstore.
steps.post: I always feel at home in this old bookstore.

steps.instr: Say it another way: complete the second sentence with the word in capitals, so it means the same.
steps.o: I don't hate my new job at all. In fact, the opposite is true: I love it.
steps.pre: I don't hate my new job at all.
steps.n: Quite the contrary = the opposite is true; it follows a negative (“don't hate”)

steps.instr: What would you say? Say it aloud, then tap the yellow box to check.
steps.sit: In a busy café, a man points at the empty chair at your table: “Mind if I sit here?” You don't mind.
steps.note: or: No, not at all. / Sure, go ahead. — not “Yes, of course”: it can sound like “Yes, I do mind!”

steps.instr: What would you say? Say it aloud, then tap the yellow box to check.
steps.sit: Your colleague fixes a huge spreadsheet in ten seconds with a trick you've never seen.
steps.ans: Wow! Could you **explain to me** how you did that?
steps.note: explain something to somebody: “explain to me how…”, “explain it to me”; not “explain me”

steps.instr: What would you say? Say it aloud, then tap the yellow box to check.
steps.sit: Your friend has worked from home all week. She hasn't left home in three days. What does she need to do?
steps.ans: You need to **get out of the house**! Even a walk around the block helps.
steps.note: get out of the house = leave home; “go out” = usually to have fun in the evening

steps.instr: What would you say? Say it aloud, then tap the yellow box to check.
steps.sit: Your friend shows you her new, very short haircut. You like it, but it's a big change, and you want to say so kindly.
steps.ans: **Don't get me wrong**, I love it, but it's a big change!
steps.note: Don't get me wrong = please don't misunderstand me; then comes the “but” part

steps.instr: What would you say? Say it aloud, then tap the yellow box to check.
steps.sit: A friend asks why you've signed up for three online courses this month. (Your kids are at their grandparents' for the whole month.)
steps.ans: The kids are away, so I've got a lot of **time on my hands**.
steps.note: or: …so I have a lot of time on my hands · “on”, not “in”

steps.instr: What would you say? Say it aloud, then tap the yellow box to check.
steps.sit: Someone asks why you still volunteer at the food bank every Saturday, even when you're tired.
steps.ans: **I can't explain it, but** it **makes me feel part of something**.
steps.note: or: a part of something; not “the part of”
